story.title: Bleached corals thrive within days when touching healthy neighbour

draft:
Bleached corals can bounce back in days—if they touch a healthy neighbor.

I just read a Nature report that a simple physical connection between a bleached colony and a thriving one can transfer symbiotic algae and nutrients, sparking rapid recovery. The experiment showed measurable growth and pigment restoration within 48 hours, suggesting that coral resilience may hinge on direct tissue sharing as much as on water quality.

What this means for restoration is profound. Instead of relying solely on large‑scale seeding or temperature control, we could design “coral bridges” that let stressed patches graft onto robust ones, accelerating natural healing. It also raises a modeling challenge: can AI predict optimal pairing strategies across reef networks to maximize recovery rates?

If we start treating reefs as interconnected living fabrics rather than isolated units, could we scale this approach globally? I’d love to hear thoughts on practical deployment or data‑driven planning for such interventions.
